To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method for the derivation of conformance tests from formal specifications that exploits the structure of specifications, and that we have developed and implemented a prototype test generator for a subset of the SDL language.

(1) The method is applicable to any protocol that can be specified in a formal language that supports a certain set of operators, (2) The method generates a test suite that is complete with respect to the set of test goals, i.e., it is complete in the sense that the test suite contains a test for each test goal, (3) The method is parameterized by two parameters: a test goal parameter and a test coverage parameter.

we developed a method for the derivation of test suites based on exploiting the formal specifications of a system under test, and that we developed a prototype tool which implements the method and which has been applied successfully in a case study.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for deriving test suites from formal specifications.
the derivation of a test suite for a protocol implementation from a formal specification of the protocol in a process algebra.
the following questions: How can we exploit structure information in order to derive test cases?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented here is a very useful tool for deriving conformance test suites.
the paper provides an interesting and promising contribution to the field of test generation.
the method proposed in this paper provides a new approach to the test derivation problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method and tools that allow the test designer to control the number, size, and complexity of the tests generated.
our method can be used to generate test suites with a given coverage and a given size.
we have developed an approach that is based on the structure of the specification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of a formal specification is a valuable source of information for test generation, and can be used to guide the generation of a small number of relevant test cases.
by using a structure-aware method, a test designer can obtain a smaller test set, which is more suitable to be used for testing.

by exploiting structure information, it is possible to derive conformance test suites that can be adjusted to different testing purposes, and to derive test suites with different characteristics in terms of test coverage and test size.
